mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) indicates an easing monetary policy, which reduces the discount rate applied to equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in periods with a sustained 3-month decline in FEDFUNDS are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) exceeds 4.5%, it signals an aggressive monetary tightening cycle that increases discount rates and compresses equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in less than 60% of triggered instances (FEDFUNDS > 4.5), or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the labor force employment (PAYEMS) is increasing and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is decreasing simultaneously, it signals a strengthening labor market that supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint condition (PAYEMS rising and UNRATE falling) occurs in more than 40% of instances but is associated with negative 20-day returns in more than 50% of those instances, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a housing market recovery (HOUST > 1000), the S&P 500 tends to have positive forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to increased consumer confidence and spending.
failure_condition: In periods where HOUST > 1000, the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in less than 60% of instances, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the CPI (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 3.0%, it signals a high-inflation environment that triggers monetary policy tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5-day returns in less than 60% of triggered instances (CPIAUCSL > 3.0), or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in industrial production (INDPRO) signals a weakening economy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 60-day forward returns in periods with a sustained 3-month decline in INDPRO are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is rising and the CPI (CPIAUCSL) is rising above 3.0%, it signals an aggressive monetary tightening cycle that increases discount rates and compresses equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint condition (FEDFUNDS rising and CPIAUCSL > 3.0) occurs in more than 40% of instances but is associated with positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of those instances, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a high-inflation regime (CPIAUCSL > 3.0), the S&P 500 tends to have negative forward returns over the next 60 trading days due to the expectation of aggressive monetary policy.
failure_condition: In periods where CPIAUCSL > 3.0, the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in less than 60% of instances, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.
